nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, the ideal period word $d_n$ contains exactly $2^{n-1}$ blocks $2, 2$, and the number $c_n$ of its blocks $2, 1, 1$ satisfies $3 c_n = 2^n - (-1)^n$; that is, $c_n = (2^n + 1)/3$ for odd $n$ and $c_n = (2^n - 1)/3$ for even $n$.
nodes.title: Block counts of the ideal period words

nodes.summary: Writing $a$ for the block $2, 1, 1$ and $b$ for the block $2, 2$ of partial quotients, the ideal period word $d_5$ is $d_4$ followed by the blocks $abb\,ab\,ab\,abb\,ab\,ab$, in this order.
nodes.title: The fifth ideal period word

nodes.summary: The digit strings of the ideal period words $d_1, d_2, d_3, d_4, d_5$ have lengths $5, 7, 17, 31, 65$ respectively.
nodes.title: Lengths of the first ideal period words

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, the digit string of the ideal period word $d_n$ (the concatenation of its blocks of partial quotients) has length $|d_n| = 2^{n+1} - (-1)^n$.

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 1$, the ideal period word $d_n$ is a finite list of blocks of partial quotients, each block being $a = 2, 1, 1$ or $b = 2, 2$. nodes.title: Ideal period words

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a natural number and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be real numbers with $x \ne \alpha$. Then the digit of $x$ for the $N$-expansion map on $[\alpha, \alpha + 1]$ is $\lfloor N/x - \alpha \rfloor$.
nodes.title: The digit away from the left endpoint

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a natural number and $\alpha$ a real number, and write $I_\alpha = [\alpha, \alpha + 1]$. The digit of a real number $x$ is $d(x) = \lfloor N/x - \alpha \rfloor$, except that when $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer, the digit of $\alpha$ itself is $d(\alpha) = N/\alpha - \alpha - 1$.
nodes.title: Digit of the N-expansion map

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a natural number and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be real numbers with $x \ne \alpha$. Then the $N$-expansion map $T_\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha \le T_\alpha(x) < \alpha + 1$.
nodes.title: The N-expansion map away from the left endpoint

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a natural number and $\alpha$ a real number such that $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer, with the convention $N/0 = 0$. Then the $N$-expansion map $T_\alpha$ satisfies $T_\alpha(\alpha) = \alpha + 1$.
nodes.title: The left endpoint goes to the right endpoint when $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$ and a real number $\alpha$, the $N$-expansion map is $T_\alpha(x) = N/x - d_\alpha(x)$ for real $x$, where $d_\alpha(x)$ is the $N$-expansion digit: $d_\alpha(x) = \lfloor N/x - \alpha \rfloor$, except that $d_\alpha(\alpha) = \lfloor N/\alpha - \alpha \rfloor - 1$ when $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
